Getting started

Getting started

The laptop mover helps you carry your own work from an old laptop to a new one. It reads what you choose, packs it into encrypted parts, and, on the new laptop, puts everything back where it was and writes a report of what is left for you to do. It runs on your own computer only, in a page at 127.0.0.1, and it uploads nothing: you do the upload yourself.

It is for any Accenture employee. You need Windows 11, a Command Prompt or PowerShell window, and about an hour of your time, most of it waiting.

What the mover moves

  • Folders you tick: copied whole, to the same path on the new laptop, minus folders that can be rebuilt (node_modules, build output, caches, .temp).
  • Git repositories: cloned again from their remote on the new laptop. Your unpushed commits and stashes travel as a git bundle, and your uncommitted files are copied. A repository with no remote is copied whole.
  • Applications: installed again on the new laptop, one by one, with winget or a signed vendor installer. Software Center apps are listed for you to install there.
  • Settings you tick: editor extensions, global npm packages and the settings files of the apps you chose.
  • Junctions: recreated.

What the mover never moves

  • Secrets. Files such as .env, .npmrc, SSH keys, certificates, cloud credentials, tokens and browser logins are never copied, even if you ticked their folder. They are listed on the by-hand list for you to set up again yourself.
  • Credentials stored by Windows (Credential Manager, the Windows secret store) and saved Wi-Fi keys.
  • Printers. Secure print queues (Pharos Secure Print) come from the company setup on the new laptop: you check that one page prints.
  • Client repositories that have a remote. They stay out of the bundle: you push, then clone again.

The four parts

  1. Scan and choose on the old laptop. Nothing is changed.
  2. Dry run and pack: see size and time first, then pack with a password you type twice.
  3. Upload the bundle to your Accenture OneDrive, and download it on the new laptop.
  4. Restore and check on the new laptop: one page, then a report.

Start the mover

On the old laptop, open PowerShell in the kit folder of the mover and run:

node kit.mjs ui

The page opens in your default browser through a one-time link. The mover stops when you close the page, press End the mover. Use --no-open to have the link printed instead of opened.

Before the move

Do these on the old laptop, in this order. Most of the later trouble comes from skipping one of them.

1. Push your repositories

The mover does not push or fetch, and it never changes a repository. A repository with a remote is cloned again on the new laptop, so what is not on the remote must be pushed first, or it travels as a local bundle.

  • For every repository you care about, push the branches you work on.
  • Unpushed commits and stashes still travel in the bundle as a safety net, but a pushed branch is the safe copy.

2. Client repositories and the client part rule

Client data is never mixed with the rest, and never leaves Accenture's own space.

  • A client repository with a remote stays out of the bundle. The dry run lists it under Push first. Push its work, then clone it again on the new laptop.
  • A client repository without a remote, or a client folder, goes into a separate encrypted client part, client-*.7z.*. Upload that part to your Accenture OneDrive only.
  • Never put any part on a client's OneDrive (its folder name usually carries the client's name) or on a personal drive. The mover refuses to write its output into a client's folder or OneDrive.

Which folders and remotes count as client data is set in a small local file, laptop-move-client.json, next to your selection file. Ask your project lead if you are unsure; without the file the mover stops, unless you confirm that nothing on this laptop is client data.

Client rules file. The mover itself names no client. The file lists client folders and remote address patterns, and the folders where output must never be written.

3. Know your secrets: the by-hand list

These are never copied. Make your own list now, and set each up again on the new laptop yourself, the safe way for what it is:

ItemWhat to do on the new laptop
SSH keys (.ssh)Create new keys, or restore them from your approved secret store, and register the new public key again.
.env files and tokensCreate the values again from their source. Do not email or upload them.
.npmrc, .pypirc, Maven settings.xmlSign in to the registry again and create a new token.
Cloud credentials (AWS, Azure, kube)Sign in again with the company tool.
Browser loginsSign in to Edge and Chrome with your account and let them sync. Profiles are never copied.
Git credentialsGit Credential Manager asks you to sign in the first time you clone from each host.
Certificates and password vault filesImport them again from where you keep them.
PrintersCheck that your secure print queue is there and that one page prints.
Wi-FiThe office network usually comes with the company image. Check it, and join other networks by hand.

The page builds this list for you from your selection and from the files the dry run finds. You tick each item when it is done.

4. Time and space

  • Space on the old laptop: a local folder (not a OneDrive folder) with room for about the size of your chosen data, a little more to be safe. The dry run shows the exact size.
  • Space on the new laptop: room for the downloaded bundle, plus a work folder of about 1.3 times the bundle size on a local drive. The restore checks this and says so before it starts.
  • Time: the dry run estimates packing, upload (at 10 MB per second) and unpacking. For a few GB it is minutes; for tens of GB expect a long lunch. Plug both laptops in.
  • Tools: 7-Zip 26.03 or newer (installed at C:\Program Files\7-Zip\7z.exe). On the new laptop the restore installs it for you if it is missing.
Tip. Close big programs before packing, and do not work in the folders while they are being packed.

Packing on the old laptop

Old laptop, step 1: scan

The scan only reads. It lists folders, applications, settings and repositories so you can choose what moves. It never pushes, fetches or locks a repository, and it never shows a remote's address.

  1. Start the page with node kit.mjs ui (see Getting started).
  2. If you saved a selection earlier, Load it on the start page: the scan is then optional. Otherwise press Start: scan this laptop.
  3. Leave Where to look empty to scan your user folder and the system drive, or give one folder per line.
  4. Keep Ask winget which applications are installed ticked to get the application list. It takes a minute.
  5. Press Scan now and wait for the status to read done.
You can stop and come back: the page keeps the scan result until you press End.

Old laptop, step 2: choose what moves

Four screens, one for each kind of thing. On each, tick what moves; the line under the table counts your choices. Every row says what will happen to it on the new laptop.

Folders

A folder is copied whole to the same path on the new laptop. Folders that hold secrets are never copied: they go on the by-hand list. Sizes come with the dry run.

Repositories

A repository with a remote is cloned again, with your local commits, stashes and uncommitted files put back. A client repository with a remote stays out of the bundle: push it first. One without a remote goes into the separate client part.

Applications

Each application shows how it will be installed: winget, a signed vendor download, or Software Center. Software Center and Company Portal apps are only listed: install them there. A vendor installer on the new laptop is run only when its signature is valid and matches the recorded publisher.

Settings

Tick the settings you want carried. Two things are not moved at all and are shown on this screen as checks for the new laptop: printers (secure print queues) and Wi-Fi (no profile or key is packed).

Old laptop, step 3: the by-hand list

These items are never copied. For each one, move it the safe way for what it is, or create it again on the new laptop, then tick it. The ticks stay in the page only.

  1. Read the list. It holds the secret folders and files in your selection, the printer check and the Wi-Fi check.
  2. Run the dry run (next page) to add the secret-bearing files it finds inside your chosen folders.
  3. Under Save the selection, give a full path ending in .json and press Save the selection. An existing file is kept as a dated .bak.json copy. The page never saves into a client's folder or a OneDrive folder.
Never copy these files into the bundle yourself, and never send them by email or chat. Keep your own list for the new laptop.

Old laptop, step 4: the dry run

The dry run shows what packing would do. Nothing is written.

  1. Give an output folder on a local drive, for example C:\LaptopMove\bundle. It must be new or empty, and not inside a OneDrive folder: you upload the files yourself.
  2. Leave part size empty for 4 GB parts, or give a size such as 500m.
  3. Tick Carry client repositories whole only if your lead asks for it. They still go only into the separate client part.
  4. Press Run the dry run and wait for finished: ready to pack.

Read the result

PartWhat it tells you
Data part, Kit zipSizes and number of parts. The kit zip holds the mover, the manifest and the signed node.exe.
TimeAn estimate of packing, upload and unpacking.
Applications, by routeHow each application will be installed.
Folders and files, RepositoriesWhat goes in and what is left out.
WarningsAnything to know, such as a missing client rules file.
Push firstClient repositories with local work: push them before you pack.
Your own steps on the new laptopThe checks and by-hand items for later.
If the dry run lists anything under Push first, do it now, then run the dry run again.

Old laptop, step 5: the password

Every part is encrypted with 7-Zip AES-256, file names too. You choose one password for all parts.

  1. Type a long passphrase in both fields. It must have at least 12 characters, and only letters, digits, spaces and the signs of a US keyboard, so it types the same on any keyboard (no accented letters).
  2. The three rules under the fields turn green when they hold. Pack now stays grey until they all do.
  3. Write the password down somewhere safe, away from the bundle (your approved password manager is the right place). Nobody can recover it.
Never put the password in the bundle folder, in an email or on OneDrive. The mover sends it from the page to 7-Zip through a pipe: it is never in a file, a log, a command line or an address, and the mover keeps no copy.

Old laptop, step 6: pack

  1. On the password page press Pack now. The page moves to Packing progress.
  2. Wait. The steps (settings, bundles of local commits, file lists, 7-Zip, checksums, the kit zip) turn done one by one, and each part has its own bar.
  3. When the green box says Packed, press Open the folder to see the bundle.

What is in the bundle folder

FileWhat it is
data-*.7z.001, .002, ...The encrypted data parts.
client-*.7z.*The separate encrypted client part, if there is one. Accenture OneDrive only.
laptop-move-kit.zipThe mover, the manifest, a README and the signed node.exe. Not encrypted: it holds no data.
SHA256SUMS.txt, manifest.jsonChecksums and the list of what is inside.

Do not rename, split or delete any of these files. You can close the page now; the mover stops when it is closed.

Uploading

Upload and download

The mover does not upload anything. You put the bundle on your own Accenture OneDrive, where you can reach it from the new laptop.

FilesWhere they go
Data parts, kit zip, checksums, manifestYour Accenture OneDrive only.
The client partYour Accenture OneDrive only. Never a client's OneDrive, never a personal drive.
The passwordNowhere. Keep it in your password manager.

Steps

  1. Open OneDrive in your browser, signed in with your Accenture account.
  2. Create a folder named move.
  3. Drag every file of the bundle folder in, the kit zip too.
  4. Wait until each file shows a green tick. Large files can take long: leave the laptop plugged in and awake.
Check the account. Your computer may also hold a client's OneDrive folder. The upload target must say Accenture. If you are not sure, upload through the browser, signed in with your Accenture account.

On the new laptop

  1. Sign in to your Accenture OneDrive in the browser and open the move folder.
  2. Download every file into one new local folder, for example C:\move. Do not use a synced OneDrive folder as the work place.
  3. Check that every file has its full size before you go on (see Troubleshooting if a checksum fails later).

Restoring on the new laptop

New laptop: restore

Do this on the new laptop, signed in as yourself. You do not need administrator rights for the mover itself, and you must not change the PowerShell execution policy: nothing here needs it.

Get the files

  1. Download the kit zip and all the parts from your Accenture OneDrive into one new folder, for example C:\move.
  2. Right-click laptop-move-kit.zip and choose Extract All, into the same folder. You get a laptop-move-kit folder with node.exe inside.
  3. Open PowerShell in that folder (in File Explorer, right-click in the folder and choose Open in Terminal).
  4. Start the mover:
.\node.exe kit.mjs ui
If company policy blocks the bundled node.exe, install Node from Software Center or with winget, then run node kit.mjs ui instead.

Check, then restore

  1. The page opens on the restore screen and shows what the bundle is: where and when it was packed, and how many parts.
  2. Fill Folder with the downloaded parts (C:\move) and Work folder for unpacking (a local drive with room, about 1.3 times the bundle size).
  3. Press Check first (nothing is written). It checks every part against its checksum and the free space, and shows what the restore would do. Fix anything under Fix these first.
  4. Tick the options you need: Skip the applications, Skip the client part, or Overwrite files that already exist. By default a file that already exists is kept and listed as a conflict.
  5. Type the bundle's password and press Restore now. Confirm the question.

While it runs

The page moves to Restore progress. The mover works in this order: check the checksums, check 7-Zip (installed for you if missing), unpack the parts, install the applications one by one, clone the repositories again and put back their local commits, stashes and files, put the folders and settings back at the same paths, and recreate the links.

An application is installed only when its signature is valid and matches the publisher recorded at packing time. If the restore stops, run it again: it continues where it stopped.

Without the page

.\node.exe kit.mjs restore --from C:\move --dry-run
.\node.exe kit.mjs restore --from C:\move

7-Zip then asks for the password in the console. To try a restore without touching real places, add --target-root C:\LaptopMove\trial --skip-apps.

Reading the report

When the restore ends, the Final report screen shows the result, and Open the report as HTML opens the same report as a page you can keep or print.

The three counters

TagMeaningWhat you do
doneRestored and checked.Nothing.
to do by handSkipped, not moved on purpose, or needs you.Do it from Your own steps now.
failedA part is damaged or missing, an app was refused, or a conflict kept your file.See Troubleshooting.

The sections

  • Parts: each part with its size and whether its SHA-256 matched.
  • Applications: installed, already there, listed for Software Center, or refused.
  • Repositories: cloned, whether the local-commit bundle was fetched, and what was put back.
  • Folders and settings: where each went, how many files moved, how many were replaced.
  • Files that already existed: kept as they were. The old laptop's copy stays in the work folder; run the restore again with Overwrite to replace them (each replaced file is backed up first).
  • Warnings: things to know, such as a missing client rules file.
  • Your own steps now: the by-hand list, the printer check, the Wi-Fi check, signing in to Edge and Chrome, and Git signing in on first clone.

After the report

  1. Work through Your own steps now and tick off your by-hand list.
  2. Clone the client repositories you pushed before the move.
  3. Print one page on the secure printer and open one repository to be sure.
  4. Delete the bundle from OneDrive and the work folder from the new laptop when you are satisfied. Keep the password until then.

Help

Troubleshooting

A checksum fails

The page says a part is damaged or its SHA-256 does not match. A part was not downloaded completely or was changed.

  1. Download that part again from OneDrive, and compare its size with the one on OneDrive.
  2. Run Check first again.

Never unpack a part that failed its check. If it fails again, the file on OneDrive may be incomplete: upload that part again from the old laptop.

An application will not install

  • Refused for its signature: the installer's signature is not valid or does not match the recorded publisher. This is on purpose. Install that application from the vendor's own page or from Software Center.
  • Software Center apps: these are only listed. Open Software Center and install them there.
  • Anything else: run the restore again (it continues where it stopped), or run only the installs with .\node.exe kit.mjs apps. You can also skip the applications and install them later.

winget is missing

winget comes with App Installer. Open the Microsoft Store (or Software Center), install or update App Installer, open a new PowerShell window, and run winget --version. If it prints a version, run the restore again. Applications with a signed vendor download are installed without winget; the others are listed for you to install by hand.

7-Zip says the password is wrong

Type it again with care for capital letters and spaces. On the console 7-Zip lets you try three times. The same message can mean a damaged part: check the checksums first. The password cannot be recovered; without it the bundle cannot be opened.

Not enough space

  • Old laptop: choose an output folder on a drive with more room, or untick large folders.
  • New laptop: the check names the drive and the room needed (about 1.3 times the bundle size). Free some space or choose another work folder on a bigger local drive, then check again.

The page says the mover has ended

The mover stops when you close its page, or press End the mover. Run node kit.mjs ui (or .\node.exe kit.mjs ui) again for a new page.

The page will not open, or says it needs the link

The link works once. Close the old tab and start the mover again, or use --no-open and paste the printed link into your browser.

The output folder is refused

It is inside a OneDrive folder or a client folder. Pick a plain local folder such as C:\LaptopMove\bundle.

A repository did not clone

Sign in when Git Credential Manager asks, and check you are on the right network or VPN. Run the restore again; repositories already cloned are kept.

Still stuck? Keep the report and the text of the error and ask your IT support. Never send the password or the bundle.

Questions and answers

Who can use it?

Any Accenture employee, on a Windows laptop, with no administrator rights needed for the mover itself.

Is my password stored anywhere?

No. You type it into the page; it goes to 7-Zip through a pipe and is never stored, logged or put in a command line, a file or an address.

Where do I upload the bundle?

To your Accenture OneDrive only. Never a client's OneDrive, never a personal drive. The client part also only to your Accenture OneDrive.

What about client repositories?

With a remote: they stay out, you push first and clone again. Without a remote: a separate encrypted client part for your Accenture OneDrive only.

Are my passwords, keys and tokens moved?

No. They are listed on the by-hand list for you to set up again. Nothing is read from the Windows secret store.

Are printers and Wi-Fi moved?

No. Secure print queues come from the company setup on the new laptop: check that one page prints. No Wi-Fi profile or key is packed: check that the office network is there.

Does it change my repositories?

No. It does not push or fetch, and it reads git without locks.

Does it change anything on the old laptop?

It writes only the bundle folder you name, and your selection file if you save it (the old one is kept as a .bak.json copy). Nothing is deleted or changed on the old laptop.

Can I try it first?

Yes. The dry run changes nothing, and --target-root restores into a trial folder instead of the real places.

Can I move only some things?

Yes. You choose folders, repositories, applications and settings. Save the selection and load it later.

How long does it take?

The dry run gives an estimate. Most of the time is waiting for the upload and download.

Why are some files left out?

Folders that can be rebuilt (node_modules, build output, caches) are skipped to keep the bundle small. Secret-bearing files are left out on purpose.

What if the restore stops half way?

Run it again. It continues where it stopped, and keeps files that already exist.

Can I use another place, such as a USB stick?

The guide supports Accenture OneDrive only.

Who can I ask?

Your IT support, with the report in hand. IT can read the security page.

Security notes for IT

This page describes what the laptop mover reads, writes and never touches, so that IT can review it. The mover is a small Node.js program with no outside dependencies. Its source is in the repository and its tests run offline.

Summary

QuestionAnswer
What does it do?Packs chosen folders, repository state, settings and an application list into encrypted parts on a local folder, and restores them on another laptop.
Does it upload anything?No. The user uploads the bundle to their Accenture OneDrive by hand. The tool never writes into a OneDrive folder or a client's folder.
Are credentials moved?No. Secret-bearing files and folders are never copied, even if ticked. They are listed for the user to set up again.
Does it read the OS secret store?No. It does not use DPAPI, Windows Credential Manager, cmdkey, keytar or the Keychain, and it exports no Wi-Fi profile or key.
Does it bypass anything?No. It needs no administrator rights, never changes the execution policy and never starts PowerShell with a bypass. Its PowerShell calls use -NoProfile -NonInteractive and only read a file's signature.
What executables does it run?The signed portable node.exe shipped in the kit (or the user's own Node), the installed 7-Zip 26.03 or newer at C:\Program Files\7-Zip\7z.exe, git, winget, reg and Windows PowerShell for signature checks. Vendor installers run only if the Authenticode signature is valid and matches the publisher recorded at packing time.
Encryption7-Zip AES-256 with encrypted file names. One password for all parts, typed by the user twice in the page.
IntegritySHA-256 of every part, recorded at packing and checked before anything is unpacked.

What it reads

  • The folders and repositories the user ticked, and the scan roots the user gave (default: the user folder and the system drive, names and sizes only).
  • Git state, read only: branches, remotes, unpushed commits, stashes, uncommitted files. Git runs with optional locks off and never fetches, pulls, pushes or changes a ref on the old laptop.
  • The list of installed applications from winget list, and the user's PATH from the registry (reg query).
  • The selection file and the local client rules file, if present.

What it writes

  • Old laptop: the bundle folder the user names, with its own staging folder; the selection file if the user saves it, with a dated .bak.json copy of an older one. Nothing is deleted or changed in the user's folders or repositories.
  • New laptop: a work folder for unpacking; the restored folders, settings and repositories at their original paths; backups of any file it replaces; junctions; an HTML report. If it installs a portable tool, it adds that folder to the user's PATH (HKCU\Environment) and nothing else in the registry.
  • Applications installed through winget or a signed vendor installer, with the user's own rights.

Network

  • The page: served on 127.0.0.1 only, on a free port, behind a one-time link that is swapped for an HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict cookie, plus a per-session key header. Requests with another Host or Origin are refused. A strict content security policy allows only the page's own files, with no outside scripts or fonts. The mover stops when the page closes or the user presses End.
  • Old laptop: none started by the tool, apart from winget's own lookups if the user asks for the application list.
  • New laptop: winget, git clone from the repositories' own remotes (the user signs in through Git Credential Manager), and, for a few tools, a vendor download over https that is checked against the vendor's published checksum and signature.
  • The tool uploads nothing, and sends no telemetry.

The password

The user types it into the page. The page sends it to the mover on 127.0.0.1, and the mover pipes it to 7-Zip's standard input. It is never on a command line, in a file, in a log or in an address, and the mover keeps no copy after the step. It is never uploaded, and it cannot be recovered: if lost, the bundle cannot be opened. Without the page, 7-Zip asks for it at its own console prompt and the mover never sees it.

Client data

  • Client repositories with a remote stay out of the bundle.
  • Client folders and repositories without a remote go into a separate encrypted client part for the user's Accenture OneDrive only.
  • The tool refuses to write its output into a client folder or a client's OneDrive, as set in the local client rules file. The tool itself names no client.

What it never touches

  • Credentials of any kind, the Windows secret store, browser profiles and passwords, saved Wi-Fi keys.
  • Other users' folders, system settings, services, scheduled tasks, firewall, drivers and policies.
  • The execution policy, UAC, or any administrator-only setting.
  • A client's OneDrive or any cloud drive other than the user's own Accenture OneDrive, which the user, not the tool, uses.

Review it yourself

The repository holds the source and its tests (npm test), and a check that drives the page in Edge on sample data. Run the dry run to see exactly what would be packed, with nothing written.
